families.notes: WHAT values carry their magnitude in the final digits and must not be truncated. The base-band and stereo-channel variants (0/10, 3/13, 20/23, 30/33, 50/53) address the same operations on different signal paths; captured F441M installations use the stereo-channel set. Relative WHAT operations and absolute DIMENSION values are complementary: prefer a reported value over counting increments.
families.evidence: WHAT, WHERE and DIMENSION tables from WHO_16.pdf v1.0.1 and the OpenWebNet Encyclopedia page functional/who-16-sound-system. The 1ES routing form and the EA amplifier decomposition are corroborated from captures on two independent F441M installations and documented in the Encyclopedia under reverse-engineering/sound-matrix-routing.md; they are not in the published specification.

families.name: Sound Diffusion
families.description: The later sound diffusion dialect. Sources, speakers, areas and general targets are structured addresses, and operation parameters are embedded in WHAT. Covers power, volume, tone, balance, 3D, loudness and presets, plus tuner frequency, modulation, stored stations, tracks and RDS. It is a separate dialect from WHO 16: similar terms do not imply compatible numeric values, address forms or parameter layouts.
families.addressing: WHERE is a tagged target class, not a decimal number with punctuation: source 2#SOURCE_ID; speaker 3#AREA#POINT; speaker area 4#AREA; general 5#SENDER_ADDRESS; all sources 6. Source dimension requests use the general-source form 5#2#SOURCE_ID while some responses use 2#SOURCE_ID, so retain the reported address rather than requiring textual equality. Keep the structure intact.

families.notes: Most commands are parameterized: a decoder must retain the entire WHAT field, because the operation and its magnitude, multimedia type and area live there. Follow Me (34) is a separate operation from ordinary ON and should not be normalized to it; 35 carries routing intent by selecting a source while turning an amplifier on. Absolute DIMENSION state complements relative WHAT operations; prefer reported values over reconstructing state from increments. One MH200N has been observed reporting every WHO 16 sound event a second time in this dialect, which is established for that device only.
families.known_source_inconsistencies: The published specification is not uniformly reliable as a copy-and-send catalogue: speaker power examples omit separators that the address table uses; speaker writes for dimensions 1-4 join the dimension marker to WHERE without the usual *; preset commands 55 and 56 contain an early ##; some tone responses disagree with the requested tone dimension; RDS commands 31 and 32 are printed without a normal WHERE; and WHAT 21 source notifications appear outside the summary table. Preserve these as source discrepancies rather than silently repairing them. Occasional trailing empty fields in volume reports should be preserved by a parser.
families.evidence: WHAT, WHERE, parameter and DIMENSION tables from WHO_22.pdf v1.1.0 and the OpenWebNet Encyclopedia page functional/who-22-sound-diffusion, which records where the specification's summary table and detailed flows disagree. The dual-dialect observation is documented in the Encyclopedia under reverse-engineering/sound-matrix-routing.md.
